title: Indian Railways Approves Provision of Kavach Version 4.0 on 660 Route Km of Izzatnagar Division of North Eastern Railway at ₹295 crore
body_text:
Indian Railways has approved the provision of Kavach Version 4.0 on 660 Route Km of the Izzatnagar Division of North Eastern Railway (NER) at an estimated cost of ₹295 crore.
The work has been approved under the umbrella work “Provision of Kavach with communication backbone of Long-Term Evolution (LTE) on balance sections of Indian Railways.”
Kavach is India's indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system designed to prevent Signal Passed at Danger (SPAD) incidents and train collisions through continuous monitoring of train movements. The system automatically applies brakes whenever required, enables trains to safely operate at maximum permissible speeds, improves operational reliability and supports safe train operations even during adverse weather conditions such as dense fog.
The approved work covers the balance sections of the Izzatnagar Division of North Eastern Railway. The provision of Kavach Version 4.0 will further strengthen the safety infrastructure on the identified railway sections.
*****
Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Vikas Jha

enrichment.summary: Indian Railways has sanctioned installation of Kavach Version 4.0, the indigenous Automatic Train Protection system, across 660 route km of the Izzatnagar Division of North Eastern Railway at an estimated cost of ₹295 crore. The work falls under the broader project of equipping balance sections of Indian Railways with Kavach along with an LTE-based communication backbone. Kavach aims to prevent Signal Passed at Danger incidents and train collisions by continuously monitoring train movement and automatically applying brakes when needed.
enrichment.context:
Kavach is India's home-grown Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system, developed by the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) with Indian vendors, positioned as a Made-in-India alternative to European ATP systems like ETCS. It gained national prominence after major railway accidents highlighted the need for automated safety mechanisms that reduce human error, particularly SPAD-related collisions. The system enables continuous train control, automatic braking, and safer operation during low-visibility conditions such as fog, which is a major cause of delays and accidents in northern India during winter.

The government has been progressively expanding Kavach coverage across zones as part of a larger safety modernization push, often linked to Mission Raftaar and overall railway safety enhancement programmes. The shift to Kavach 4.0 with an LTE-based communication backbone reflects an upgrade path enabling better interoperability, higher data transmission capabilities, and readiness for increased traffic density and higher speeds. Approvals like this one for the Izzatnagar Division of North Eastern Railway are part of incremental, division-wise rollouts across the country, reflecting the phased and capital-intensive nature of retrofitting India's vast rail network with modern train protection technology.
